headlines.article_text: Alphabet stock drops 10% while Microsoft rises after earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Alphabet reported a larger negative free cash flow than analysts had expected while maintaining its spending guidance for the year. Microsoft saw free cash flow fall but it remained positive ads its capex came in below expectations If Alphabet shares fall more than 9.77% on Thursday, that would be its worst post-earnings reaction ever. In this article GOGL3'A-BR MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Google headquarters in Mountain View, California, US, on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Alphabet shares were sharply down in premarket trading on Thursday while Microsoft rose as investors focused on the tech giants' latest spending and free cash flow numbers in their third-quarter earnings. Alphabet was 10% lower in premarket trade while Microsoft was nearly 4% higher. If Alphabet closes more than 9.77% lower on Thursday, it would be its worst post-earnings reaction ever. The company went public in 2004. Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the third quarter, which was 30% higher than a year ago , but below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive. Alphabet, in contrast, reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, which fell much further than the $2.70 billion analysts expected by analysts. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion. The earnings report comes as investors scrutinize AI spending plans of tech companies and are focusing on the returns on those investments. "Microsoft is building out its architecture in a measured way and as such contains fewer surprises," Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said on Thursday. "Alphabet, by contrast, saw its share price hit after hours as a result of a fairly messy set of results and a poorly handled earnings call," Barringer added. Nasdaq-100 futures were down more than 1% early Thursday. Search under pressure Alphabet's biggest source of revenue, search advertising, grew 12% in the September quarter to $63.35 billion, but missed analyst expectations, adding further pressure to the company's shares. P hilipp Schindler, Alphabet's chief business officer, said the impact on the search business was partly because of lower monetization within the company's AI Mode. He added that Alphabet is now "scaling" ads within its AI Overviews and AI Mode products, including in international markets. Google's search business has faced headwinds from the rise of other AI chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. People may be carrying out more search queries outside Google. Gemini, Google's own AI chatbot, has failed to keep pace. "The problem for Google is it faces an innovator's dilemma and doesn't know whether to protect its core business or look to join the disruption. As such, Google has lost its edge with Gemini and is behind peers on agentic AI," Barringer said. - CNBC's Robert Hum, Samantha Subin and Jordan Novet contributed reporting. headlines.article_text: Tencent, Visa broaden payments partnership after China approvals Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tencent and Visa signed an agreement to expand cooperation in cross-border payments, AI-powered commerce and international money transfers. Visa announced that it received approval to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing business in China. Citi also secured regulatory approval to establish a wholly owned securities venture in China. In this article TME V Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Thomas Fuller | Lightrocket | Getty Images Tencent and Visa are expanding their partnership in cross-border payments and AI-powered commerce, the companies said Thursday, deepening their push into China’s payments market. The agreement follows fresh regulatory approvals for U.S. financial firms in China, with Visa and Citi receiving the green light this month to expand their operations in the world’s second-largest economy. Under the memorandum of understanding, Tencent and Visa will explore ways to make payments easier for travelers entering and leaving China while expanding their cross-border money transfer partnership. The companies also plan to develop payment solutions that would allow travelers to pay participating merchants through Tencent’s Weixin Pay and Visa networks, subject to regulatory requirements. They also aim to expand their collaboration through Visa Direct, Visa’s money transfer service, making it easier for overseas users to send funds into the Weixin Pay ecosystem. The partnership will also extend to agentic commerce, an emerging form of online shopping in which AI agents can help consumers find, select and purchase products or services. Dowson Tong, Tencent's senior executive vice president and CEO of its Cloud and Smart Industries Group, said the partnership would combine Tencent's AI capabilities with Visa's global network to improve cross-border payments. "We hope to create more seamless commerce experiences for consumers and new opportunities for businesses, both in China and internationally," he said. The announcement follows Visa’s approval from the People’s Bank of China earlier this month to begin preparations for a domestic bank card clearing business, bringing it closer to entering China’s domestic payments market after more than four decades in the country. Visa and Tencent have been cooperating since at least 2019, when the U.S. payments company announced plans to allow international Visa cardholders to make payments through WeChat Pay in China. Tencent has also expanded its partnerships with other global payments firms. In December last year, Mastercard and Tencent's international payments platform Midas announced a collaboration to integrate Mastercard's Click to Pay and payment security technologies into Midas' overseas payment solutions, with the aim of making online transactions faster and more secure. Last week, Citi said it received approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission to establish a wholly owned securities company in China. The Shanghai-based venture, Citigroup Securities (China), will offer services including equities brokerage, securities underwriting, research and principal trading to domestic and international clients. Citi said it would complete the remaining regulatory procedures before beginning operations. The approvals come as Beijing continues to open parts of its financial sector to foreign companies. CNBC previously reported that U.S. officials pressed Beijing on market access for Mastercard, Visa and Citigroup during bilateral meetings in Bangkok, citing a U.S. Treasury official. The official said regulatory approvals were also part of an agreement reached by U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping during their meeting in Washington last month. headlines.title: Microsoft stock jumps 4% as cloud growth drives earnings and revenue beat
headlines.summary: Microsoft reported better-than-expected results driven by 48% growth in Azure revenue.
headlines.article_text: Microsoft (MSFT) Q1 earnings report 2027 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft reported 19% revenue growth, topping estimates. Azure cloud revenue jumped 48% to $33.2 billion. Free cash flow declined 27% from a year ago. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a company event at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on Oct. 20, 2026. Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft shares rose 4% in extended trading on Wednesday after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly results, driven by 48% growth in its Azure cloud infrastructure business. Here's how the company fared relative to LSEG consensus: Earnings per share: $4.89 adjusted vs. $4.73 expected Revenue: $92.28 billion vs. $90.69 billion expected Microsoft's revenue grew 19% year over year in the quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, according to a statement , with Azure now its biggest single business. The software giant has been rapidly building out data center infrastructure to meet artificial intelligence demand, while also maintaining positive free cash flow unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Microsoft reported $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount had projected $50.67 billion. With respect to guidance, Microsoft called for $96 billion to $97.1 billion in fiscal second-quarter revenue, which works out to 18.8% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $95.60 billion in revenue. For Azure, Microsoft's finance chief, Amy Hood, said on a conference call with analysts that she anticipates 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the fiscal second quarter, compared with the 45.1% StreetAccount consensus. "We still have demand that exceeds supply," she said. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft flagged a higher growth rate for cash paid for property and equipment than overall capital expenditures, which include finance leases. "Some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed," Hood said. Around 75% of capital expenditures are now tied to short-lived assets such as Intel chips and Nvidia graphics processing units, up from about 66% in the past three quarters and half in the year-ago quarter. The shift indicates Microsoft's prioritization of infrastructure it can can quickly turn into revenue. Hood said the company is aiming at over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures and finance leases, above the StreetAccount consensus of $53.10 billion, with $170 billion for all of calendar 2027 because of the capacity issues. "In the second half of the fiscal year, we currently expect capex spend to accelerate primarily from CPUs, inclusive of higher memory and storage costs, and GPUs, as well as the 3P capacity deliveries that shifted to H2," she said. The delays have to do with GPU-as-a-service providers, she said. Free cash flow for the fiscal first quarter declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Cloud rival Alphabet reported more than $9 billion in negative free cash flow in the quarter after Meta said last week its cash flow turned negative for the first time. Microsoft will continue to generate free cash flow through the 2027 fiscal year, but the company will access additional sources of funding when it's attractive to do so, Hood said. "We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our rates ratings are, and sort of we haven't been able to — we haven't yet, I would say, tapped that," she said. "And then, of course, there's other options." Microsoft's net income increased to $36.63 billion, or $4.92 per share, from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 per share, a year ago. Adjusted earnings exclude a roughly $200 million loss on its investment in OpenAI. For the first time, Microsoft disclosed revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars, at $33.17 billion in the quarter, despite the delays from third-party providers. Analysts polled by StreetAccount expected $32.32 billion. The growth rate in the June quarter was 42%. Microsoft reported results under two operating segments — Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer. For the past 11 years, the company had three segments that divided up its Azure, Office and Windows businesses. In Agents and Infra, revenue rose almost 25% to $76.8 billion, more than the $75.63 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount. The segment contains Azure, along with Microsoft 365 cloud products, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions and frontier and support services. The number of people using the Microsoft 365 Copilot AI assistant is up 50% from last quarter, CEO Satya Nadella said on the call. The company did not disclose the number of paid seats. The recently announced high-end Microsoft 365 E7 productivity bundle now has millions of seats, Hood said. Revenue in the Devices and Consumer business slipped 3% to $15.48 billion, beating the StreetAccount consensus of $15.05 billion. The unit includes search and advertising, Xbox, devices and Windows operating system licenses sold to device makers. Sales of devices and Windows licenses declined 22%, as higher memory and storage costs elevated prices. The company pointed to the end of support for Windows 10 last year and weak PC demand. As of Wednesday's close, Microsoft shares were up about 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained 13% over the same period. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app" with coding abilities.
